Notations

{notation:abc} A tune in ABC notation drawn as a staff. 
{notation:abc 'text'/}
{notation:braille} A text in braille: Unified English Braille, grade 1, as the characters of Unicode's braille block, the text itself the accessible name. 
{notation:braille 'text'/}
{notation:bridge} A deal of contract bridge written as the Deal tag of PBN, the Portable Bridge Notation. 
{notation:bridge 'text'/}
{notation:chem} Chemical formulas and equations, typed as chemists type them, as MathML. 
{notation:chem 'text'/}
{notation:chess} A chess position drawn as a board, the pieces shapes of PAD's own. 
{notation:chess 'fen', flip, highlight='e2, e4', arrow='e2-e4, g8-f6', size=360, title='name'/}
{notation:chord} A chord of a guitar or a ukulele as the box of a chord chart. 
{notation:chord 'text'/}
{notation:cube} A sequence of moves of a twisty cube in the notation of the World Cube Association. 
{notation:cube 'text'/}
{notation:draughts} A draughts position from the FEN of PDN, drawn as a board. 
{notation:draughts 'text'/}
{notation:go} A go position from a game record in SGF, drawn as a board. 
{notation:go 'text'/}
{notation:karnaugh} A Boolean function of two to four variables drawn as its Karnaugh map, the cells in Gray-code order with their 1s. 
{notation:karnaugh 'text'/}
{notation:math} A formula written in AsciiMath, the notation of asciimath.org, as MathML. 
{notation:math 'text'/}
{notation:morse} A text in the international Morse code of ITU-R M.1677-1. 
{notation:morse 'text'/}
{notation:piano} Notes on a piano keyboard, the keys pressed marked and named. 
{notation:piano 'text'/}
{notation:semaphore} A text in flag semaphore. 
{notation:semaphore 'text'/}
{notation:signals} A text spelt in the maritime signal flags of the International Code of Signals. 
{notation:signals 'text'/}
{notation:siteswap} A juggling pattern in siteswap notation, each throw the number of beats until the ball is thrown again. 
{notation:siteswap 'text'/}
{notation:tablature} A tab for a guitar, a bass, a ukulele or any fretted instrument, written as players write it in plain text and drawn as it is printed. 
{notation:tablature 'text'/}

Effects

{effect:confetti} A burst of confetti from where it stands. 
{effect:confetti/}
{effect:confetti}<button type="button">Celebrate</button>{/effect:confetti}
{effect:countup} A number counted up to its value by the CSS alone. 
{effect:countup to=1250/}
{effect:countup 1250/}
{effect:countup}1250{/effect:countup}
{effect:decipher} A short heading that resolves out of scrambled signs. 
{effect:decipher}ACCESS GRANTED{/effect:decipher}
{effect:decipher 'ACCESS GRANTED'/}
{effect:encircle} A ring drawn round a word or a short phrase as a pen circles it on paper. 
{effect:encircle}the one word{/effect:encircle}
{effect:encircle 'this'/}
{effect:glitch} A digital glitch: for a moment the text tears into slices that jump aside in two colours, then it stands still again. 
{effect:glitch}SIGNAL LOST{/effect:glitch}
{effect:glitch 'SIGNAL LOST'/}
{effect:gradient} Text painted with a gradient. 
{effect:gradient}Build pages, not plumbing{/effect:gradient}
{effect:gradient 'PAD'/}
{effect:highlighter} A stroke of a marker pen drawn behind the words, left to right, once. 
{effect:highlighter}the one thing to remember{/effect:highlighter}
{effect:highlighter 'this'/}
{effect:marquee} A band whose content scrolls by without end, a logo strip, a ticker. 
{effect:marquee}<span>PHP</span> <span>Go</span> <span>Rust</span>{/effect:marquee}
{effect:marquee 'Breaking: the sale ends tonight'/}
{effect:nudge} A short movement that draws the eye to something, then lets it be. 
{effect:nudge}<a class="button" href="?signup">Try it free</a>{/effect:nudge}
{effect:nudge 'New'/}
{effect:reveal} A block that comes into view as it is scrolled to. 
{effect:reveal}<div class="card">...</div>{/effect:reveal}
{effect:rotator} One place in a line where its phrases take turns. 
{effect:rotator}teams, makers, you{/effect:rotator}
{effect:rotator 'fast, simple, yours'/}
{effect:scrollprogress} A thin bar along the top of the window that fills as the reader scrolls the page, from its top to its end. 
{effect:scrollprogress/}
{effect:shimmer} A band of light that sweeps across the letters and rests, as on something freshly polished. 
{effect:shimmer}New in this release{/effect:shimmer}
{effect:shimmer 'New'/}
{effect:skeleton} A placeholder in the shape of what is still on its way, a sheen sweeping over it. 
{effect:skeleton/}
{effect:skeleton lines=4/}
{effect:skeleton shape='card'/}
{effect:spinner} A loading indicator, the one effect for every loader. 
{effect:spinner/}
{effect:spinner style='dots', label='Saving'/}
{effect:spinner}Loading the orders{/effect:spinner}
{effect:spotlight} A block lit by a soft light behind its content. 
{effect:spotlight}<h2>Introducing PAD</h2><p>...</p>{/effect:spotlight}
{effect:strike} A line drawn through the words from left to right, once. 
{effect:strike}€49{/effect:strike}
{effect:strike 'was 49'/}
{effect:tilt} A card that leans in 3D when the pointer is on it or the focus is in it, and settles again when it leaves. 
{effect:tilt}<div class="card">...</div>{/effect:tilt}
{effect:typewriter} A line of text typed out letter by letter behind a caret, once, then the caret blinks a few times and stays. 
{effect:typewriter}Hello, world{/effect:typewriter}
{effect:typewriter 'Hello, world'/}
{effect:underline} A line drawn under the words from left to right, once. 
{effect:underline}the terms{/effect:underline}
{effect:underline 'this'/}
{effect:wave} The letters rise and fall one after the other, a wave running through the word. 
{effect:wave}Hello there{/effect:wave}
{effect:wave 'Hello there'/}

JSON-LD kinds

{jsonld:article} An Article: a post of a blog, a news item, a page of a magazine, its headline, who wrote it and when. 
{jsonld:article data='post'/}
{jsonld:article headline=$title, author=$author, published=$date/}
{jsonld:breadcrumb} A BreadcrumbList: where the page stands, from the home page down, each step a ListItem numbered by its position. 
{jsonld:breadcrumb/}
{jsonld:breadcrumb data='trail'/}
{jsonld:business} A LocalBusiness: a shop, a practice, a garage. 
{jsonld:business data='shop'/}
{jsonld:business type='Bakery', name='The Loaf', street='Main Street 1', city='Utrecht', country='NL', hours='Mo-Fr 08:00-18:00; Sa 08:00-16:00'/}
{jsonld:course} A Course: a series of lessons, what it teaches and who gives it. 
{jsonld:course data='course'/}
{jsonld:course name='PAD in a day', description='The template language from the first tag to a shop.', provider='PAD Academy'/}
{jsonld:event} An Event: a concert, a course, a meeting, when it starts and where, and the tickets for it. 
{jsonld:event data='concert'/}
{jsonld:event name='PAD day', starts='2026-11-20 19:30', place='The Hall', address='Main Street 1, Utrecht'/}
{jsonld:faq} An FAQPage: the questions of a page and their answers, each a Question with its acceptedAnswer. 
{jsonld:faq data='questions'/}
{jsonld:itemlist} An ItemList: the page that lists pages of one kind. 
{jsonld:itemlist data='recipes'/}
{jsonld:job} A JobPosting: a vacancy, what the work is, who offers it, where and for what pay. 
{jsonld:job data='vacancy'/}
{jsonld:job title='Baker', description=$text, posted='2026-11-01', company='The Loaf', city='Utrecht', country='NL', employment='full time', salary='3200-3800', currency='EUR', per='month'/}
{jsonld:organization} An Organization: the company, the club or the project behind the site, its logo and its profiles elsewhere. 
{jsonld:organization name='PAD', url='https://pad.example', logo='logo.png'/}
{jsonld:person} A Person: the author of a site, a speaker, a member of a team. 
{jsonld:person name='Ann Smith', job='Engineer', profiles='https://github.com/ann'/}
{jsonld:product} A Product: a thing for sale, what it is and what it costs. 
{jsonld:product data='product'/}
{jsonld:product name='Kettle', price=$price, currency='EUR', availability='InStock'/}
{jsonld:profile} A ProfilePage: the page of one person, or one organization, on a site of many. 
{jsonld:profile data='member'/}
{jsonld:profile name='Ann Smith', handle='ann', image='avatars/ann.jpg', followers=$followers, created=$joined/}
{jsonld:recipe} A Recipe: a dish, what goes in it, how it is made and how long that takes. 
{jsonld:recipe data='recipe'/}
{jsonld:recipe name='Pea soup', image='soup.jpg', prep='20 min', cook='1 h 30 min', yield='4 servings'/}
{jsonld:restaurant} A Restaurant: a local business that serves food and drink, and what it serves. 
{jsonld:restaurant data='restaurant'/}
{jsonld:restaurant name='De Ketel', cuisine='Dutch', menu='?menu', street='Oudegracht 1', city='Utrecht', country='NL', hours='Tu-Su 17:00-23:00', prices='$$'/}
{jsonld:software} A SoftwareApplication: a program, an app, a web application. 
{jsonld:software data='app'/}
{jsonld:software name='Pocket Ledger', os='Android 12, iOS 17', category='finance', price='0', rating='4.6', ratings='1523'/}
{jsonld:video} A VideoObject: a video of the page, what it shows, when it was put there, how long it runs and where it plays. 
{jsonld:video data='video'/}
{jsonld:video name='Making pea soup', thumbnail='soup.jpg', uploaded='2026-11-01T10:00:00+01:00', duration='4 min 12 s', player=$embed/}
{jsonld:website} A WebSite: the site itself, its name and its address, and how to search it, which a search engine may offer as a search box of its own. 
{jsonld:website name='PAD', search='?search&q='/}

Validation rules

rule / accepted A box that must be ticked, terms and conditions: 1, on, yes or true, in any case. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'accepted' ], $values );
rule / after After:other - a moment strictly after another, read as before: reads it: after:start, the other field of that name, or after:2026-01-01, a date written in the rule. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'after:other' ], $values );
rule / after_or_equal After_or_equal:other - a moment after another or the same one, as after: reads them: the end of a trip of one day, after_or_equal:start, or after_or_equal:2026-01-01, a date written in the rule. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'after_or_equal:other' ], $values );
rule / alpha Letters only, of any script, with the marks that go with them: José and Zoë pass, a space, a digit or a dash does not. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'alpha' ], $values );
rule / alphanum Letters and digits only, of any script: a user name, a code without signs. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'alphanum' ], $values );
rule / before Before:other - a moment strictly before another: before:end, the other field of that name, or before:2027-01-01, a date written in the rule - one that reads as a date (four digits, a dash, a digit) is a date, whatever field the post has of that name. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'before:other' ], $values );
rule / before_or_equal Before_or_equal:other - a moment before another or the same one, as before: reads them: a start no later than the end, before_or_equal:end, or before_or_equal:2026-12-31, a date written in the rule. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'before_or_equal:other' ], $values );
rule / between Between:a,b - min:a and max:b in one rule: from a to b characters long, or on a number field a value from a to b. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'between:1,10' ], $values );
rule / color A colour written in hexadecimal, #rgb or #rrggbb, in either case: what <input type="color"> posts, and what a style sheet can be handed back as it is. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'color' ], $values );
rule / date A day of a month of a year, in any form date_parse reads without an error, that checkdate takes: 2026-02-30 is none. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'date' ], $values );
rule / different Different:field - not the same text as another field of the post, the mirror of same: a new password that is not the one in use, different:current_password. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'different:other' ], $values );
rule / digits Digits, digits:n - the digits 0 to 9 and nothing else, and with n exactly n of them: a postal code of four, a PIN of six. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'digits:4' ], $values );
rule / distinct No value is in a list twice (a field named guests[]): the addresses of the people invited, each once. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'distinct' ], $values );
rule / email An e-mail address as PHP's FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL takes one; the browser's half carries the same pattern. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'email' ], $values );
rule / ends_with Ends_with:a,b - the value ends with one of the texts of the list, as written: ends_with:.pdf,.txt for a file name, ends_with:@example.com for an address of the house. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'ends_with:.jpg,.png' ], $values );
rule / gt Gt:other - more than another field, or than a number written in the rule: a highest price above the lowest, gt:min_price, an amount above nothing, gt:0 - where min:0 takes 0. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'gt:0' ], $values );
rule / gte Gte:other - at least another field, or a number written in the rule: a highest price no lower than the lowest, gte:min_price. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'gte:0' ], $values );
rule / iban An international bank account number whose check digits hold: the country's two letters, two check digits and 11 to 30 letters and digits, the spaces it is often written with left out, in either case; moved the first four to the end and read with A as 10 to Z as 35, the number leaves 1 when divided by 97 (ISO 13616). 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'iban' ], $values );
rule / in In:a,b,c - one of the values of the list, as written: in:red,green refuses Red. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'in:red,green' ], $values );
rule / integer A whole number PHP's integers hold, as FILTER_VALIDATE_INT reads one: no leading zero, a sign allowed. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'integer' ], $values );
rule / ip Ip, ip:v4, ip:v6 - an IP address as FILTER_VALIDATE_IP reads one: four numbers of 0 to 255 without a leading zero, or the groups of IPv6 with one :: at most - of either kind, or of the one the argument names. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'ip:v4' ], $values );
rule / json A JSON text PHP reads: a settings field, a snippet of data. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'json' ], $values );
rule / lowercase Nothing that has a lower case is written in upper case: a user name, a code. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'lowercase' ], $values );
rule / lt Lt:other - less than another field, or than a number written in the rule: a discount below the price, lt:price, a share below the whole, lt:100. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'lt:100' ], $values );
rule / lte Lte:other - at most another field, or a number written in the rule: no more guests than seats, lte:seats. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'lte:100' ], $values );
rule / max Max:n - at most n characters, or on a number field a value of at most n. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'max:10' ], $values );
rule / max_items Max_items:n - a list (a field named toppings[]) of at most n values: three toppings at most, max_items:3. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'max_items:3' ], $values );
rule / max_words Max_words:n - a text of at most n words: an abstract of 250 words, max_words:250. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'max_words:20' ], $values );
rule / min Min:n - at least n characters, counted as mb_strlen counts them; on a number field - one with numeric or integer - a value of at least n. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'min:1' ], $values );
rule / min_items Min_items:n - a list (a field named toppings[]) of at least n values: two toppings or more, min_items:2. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'min_items:1' ], $values );
rule / min_words Min_words:n - a text of at least n words: a review of twenty words or more, min_words:20. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'min_words:2' ], $values );
rule / multiple_of Multiple_of:n - a number that is a whole multiple of n: packs of six, multiple_of:6, a quarter of an hour, multiple_of:0.25, whole cents, multiple_of:0.01. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'multiple_of:6' ], $values );
rule / not_in Not_in:a,b,c - none of the values of the list, as written: not_in:admin,root refuses root and takes Root, as in: reads its list. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'not_in:admin,root' ], $values );
rule / numeric A number as is_numeric reads one: 12, -1.5, 1e3, .5. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'numeric' ], $values );
rule / regex Regex:/pattern/flags - the value matches a PCRE pattern. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'regex:/^[A-Z]+$/' ], $values );
rule / required The field holds something: a text that is not empty once trimmed, a list (a field named tags[]) with at least one item filled in - three fields of guests[] left blank hold none, as no box ticked holds none. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'required' ], $values );
rule / required_if Required_if:field,value[,value...] - required, as required judges it, when another field holds one of the values, as written - case and all, as in: compares: an address when delivery is ship, required_if:delivery,ship,courier for either. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'required_if:other,yes' ], $values );
rule / required_unless Required_unless:field,value[,value...] - required, as required judges it, unless another field holds one of the values, as written: an address unless delivery is collect. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'required_unless:other,no' ], $values );
rule / required_with Required_with:field[,field...] - required, as required judges it, when one of the other fields is filled, as required judges that: a text that is not empty once trimmed, a list with an item filled in. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'required_with:other' ], $values );
rule / required_without Required_without:field[,field...] - required, as required judges it, when one of the other fields is empty - one of two ways to be reached, a phone when there is no e-mail, required_without:email. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'required_without:other' ], $values );
rule / same Same:field - the same text as another field of the post, a password typed twice. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'same:other' ], $values );
rule / slug The name of a page in an address, as padStrSlug makes one: lower case letters and digits, words joined by one dash, no dash at either end. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'slug' ], $values );
rule / starts_with Starts_with:a,b - the value begins with one of the texts of the list, as written: starts_with:https:// for a secure address, starts_with:NL,BE for a code of two countries. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'starts_with:PAD,PHP' ], $values );
rule / time A time of day on the 24-hour clock, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, the hour with one digit or two: what <input type="time"> posts, 09:30, and what a person types, 9:30. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'time' ], $values );
rule / uppercase Nothing that has an upper case is written in lower case: a country code, a licence plate. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'uppercase' ], $values );
rule / url A web address: what FILTER_VALIDATE_URL takes, and http or https - a javascript: or file: address is a URL too, and no address a visitor's link should hold. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'url' ], $values );
rule / uuid A UUID in its usual form, 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits, of any version - what padStrUuid makes - in either case. 
$errors = padValidate ( [ 'value' => 'uuid' ], $values );

OAuth providers

oauth / apple Sign in with Apple: a Services ID as APPLE_CLIENT_ID, and in place of a fixed secret a key of the developer account - APPLE_TEAM_ID, APPLE_KEY_ID and the key itself in APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY (the PEM text of the .p8 file, or its path) - from which every token exchange makes the client secret Apple asks for: an ES256 JWT, signed with openssl. 
{widget:oauth 'apple', href='#example'/}
oauth / bitbucket Log in with Bitbucket (Bitbucket Cloud): an OAuth consumer of a workspace (Settings, OAuth consumers), its key and secret in BITBUCKET_CLIENT_ID and BITBUCKET_CLIENT_SECRET, its callback URL the address of the login page, and its permissions Account: Read and Email - a consumer's scopes are set there, not asked for in the address. 
{widget:oauth 'bitbucket', href='#example'/}
oauth / discord Log in with Discord: an application of the developer portal, its id and secret in DISCORD_CLIENT_ID and DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'discord', href='#example'/}
oauth / forgejo Log in with Forgejo (or Gitea): Codeberg by default, or the forge at the address in the option base or FORGEJO_URL; an OAuth2 application's id and secret in FORGEJO_CLIENT_ID and FORGEJO_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'forgejo', href='#example'/}
oauth / github Log in with GitHub: an OAuth app (Settings, Developer settings), its client id and secret in GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'github', href='#example'/}
oauth / gitlab Log in with GitLab: an application of gitlab.com, or of a GitLab of your own with its address in the option base or GITLAB_URL; its id and secret in GITLAB_CLIENT_ID and GITLAB_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'gitlab', href='#example'/}
oauth / google Sign in with Google, OpenID Connect: a client of the Google Cloud console, its id and secret in GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'google', href='#example'/}
oauth / linkedin Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect: an app of the developer portal with that product added, its client id and secret in LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID and LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'linkedin', href='#example'/}
oauth / microsoft Sign in with Microsoft, OpenID Connect on the identity platform: an app registration's id and secret in MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID and MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, the tenant in the option tenant or MICROSOFT_TENANT - common (default: work, school and personal accounts), organizations, consumers, or a tenant's own id or domain. 
{widget:oauth 'microsoft', href='#example'/}
oauth / oidc Any OpenID Connect provider - Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel, Auth0, Okta, a company's own: its issuer in the option issuer or OIDC_ISSUER, its client in OIDC_CLIENT_ID and OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET (or another prefix with the option env='KEYCLOAK' - KEYCLOAK_ISSUER, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID ...). 
{widget:oauth 'oidc', href='#example'/}
oauth / slack Sign in with Slack, OpenID Connect: a Slack app with its redirect URL set under OAuth & Permissions, its client id and secret in SLACK_CLIENT_ID and SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'slack', href='#example'/}
oauth / x Log in with X (Twitter): a Web App of the X developer console - a confidential client, with OAuth 2.0 switched on and the login page as its callback URL - its client id and secret in X_CLIENT_ID and X_CLIENT_SECRET. 
{widget:oauth 'x', href='#example'/}

Notification channels

channel / database The notification kept on the site, for the person to read there: the {widget:notifications/} tag lists the unread ones of the user logged in, each with a link that marks it read; padNotifications and padNotificationRead do the same from PHP. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'database' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / discord A message to a Discord channel through a webhook: its address in DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL, or the option url - never a field of the recipient, as for slack. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'discord' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / gotify A message to a self-hosted Gotify server (gotify.net), which pushes it to the phones and browsers its user is signed in on: the server in GOTIFY_URL - never the recipient's - and an application's token in GOTIFY_TOKEN, sent as a bearer token in the Authorization header, which the server reads beside its own X-Gotify-Key: the header the reports redact by its name, and never the query's token=, which a proxy's log keeps. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'gotify' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / mail The notification as an e-mail, through padMail and the transport it is set up with ($padMailTransport - a file under DATA/mail/ by default): the @mail@ section, or the plain text, is the HTML part, the text part is made from it, the title is the subject. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'mail' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / matrix A message in a Matrix room, sent by a bot account: the homeserver in MATRIX_HOMESERVER (https://matrix.org; never the recipient's), the account's access token in MATRIX_TOKEN, the room - its id, !abc:matrix.org, not an alias #name - in the recipient's field matrix or MATRIX_ROOM. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'matrix' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / mattermost A message to a Mattermost channel through an incoming webhook: its address, https://<server>/hooks/<id>, in MATTERMOST_WEBHOOK_URL, or the option url - never a field of the recipient, as for slack; the id in it is its credential, which the reports redact. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'mattermost' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / ntfy A push to the phones and desktops subscribed to an ntfy topic: the topic in the recipient's field ntfy or NTFY_TOPIC - letters, digits, _ and - -, the server in NTFY_URL (https://ntfy.sh unless given; never the recipient's), an access token in NTFY_TOKEN when the topic is protected. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'ntfy' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / pushover A push to the phones and desktops of a Pushover user, or of every member of a Pushover group, through its Message API (https://pushover.net/api): the application's token in PUSHOVER_TOKEN, the user's or group's key in the recipient's field pushover or PUSHOVER_USER - each 30 letters and digits. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'pushover' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / slack A message to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook: its address in SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, or the option url - never a field of the recipient: a webhook posts to the one channel it was made for, and its address is this server's to choose. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'slack' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / sms A text message through an HTTP gateway of the generic shape: a POST to SMS_URL of JSON { "to": ..., "from": ..., "text": ... 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'sms' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / teams A message to a Microsoft Teams channel through a workflow's webhook ("Post to a channel when a webhook request is received"): its address in TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL, or the option url - never a field of the recipient, as for slack. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'teams' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / telegram A message from a Telegram bot: the bot's token in TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, the chat in the recipient's field telegram or TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID - its id, a number (negative for a group), or a channel's @name; a handle of a person is none, a bot cannot write to one. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'telegram' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / twilio A text message through Twilio's Messaging API (the Message resource of its REST API 2010-04-01): the account in TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID - AC and 32 hex digits, in the address of the resource - and its auth token in TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN as the password of HTTP basic authentication, the account's SID the user; with an API key in TWILIO_API_KEY (SK and 32) the key is the user and TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN holds its secret. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'twilio' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / webhook The notification as JSON posted to an address of the application's choosing - Zapier, n8n, a service of its own - and signed as Standard Webhooks has it (standardwebhooks.com): the address in WEBHOOK_URL, or the option url - never a field of the recipient - and the secret in WEBHOOK_SECRET, whsec_ and the base64 of 24 to 64 random bytes as the spec has a symmetric one (the prefix optional), or several split by spaces while a new one is rolled in. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'webhook' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();
channel / webpush A push message to the browsers the person allowed to notify them, also with the site closed: the recipient's field webpush holds the subscription the browser gave - PushSubscription.toJSON (), as an array or its JSON - or a list of them. 
padNotify ( $recipient, 'order-shipped', [ 'order' => 42 ], [ 'webpush' ] );
$results = padNotifyResults ();

AI providers

ai / anthropic Claude, through Anthropic's Messages API: the key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, claude-opus-5-5 unless model= names another. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='anthropic'/}
ai / bedrock Amazon Bedrock, its Converse API (docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/ API_runtime_Converse.html): POST https://bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com/model/<model>/converse, one interface for every model of Bedrock that takes messages. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='bedrock'/}
ai / cloudflare Workers AI, the models Cloudflare runs on its own network, through its REST API (developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/get-started/rest-api/): POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<account>/ai/run/<model> with the API token as a bearer token - the token in CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, the account in CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, the names Cloudflare's Wrangler reads - @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast unless model= names another of the catalogue's text generation models (@cf/<author>/<name>, @hf/... 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='cloudflare'/}
ai / cohere Cohere's Chat API v2 (POST https://api.cohere.com/v2/chat, docs.cohere.com/reference/chat): the key in COHERE_API_KEY - or CO_API_KEY, the name Cohere's own SDKs read - sent as a bearer token, command-a-plus-05-2026 unless model= names another. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='cohere'/}
ai / gemini Google's Gemini API, generateContent: the key in GEMINI_API_KEY (sent as the x-goog-api-key header, never in the address), gemini-2.5-flash unless model= names another. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='gemini'/}
ai / lmstudio A model running on this machine or the network with LM Studio, through its native REST API (lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/rest/chat, LM Studio 0.4 and later): POST http://127.0.0.1:1234/api/v1/chat - the server LM Studio starts (lms server start), url= naming another address - ibm/granite-4-micro unless model= names another downloaded model, loaded on the first request when it is not. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='lmstudio'/}
ai / mistral Mistral's chat completions: the key in MISTRAL_API_KEY, mistral-large-latest unless model= names another. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='mistral'/}
ai / ollama A model running on this machine or the network with Ollama: no key, the server at OLLAMA_HOST (http://127.0.0.1:11434 unless set), llama3.2 unless model= names another - a model pulled there first (ollama pull llama3.2). 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='ollama'/}
ai / openai OpenAI's chat completions: the key in OPENAI_API_KEY, gpt-5 unless model= names another. 
{pad:ai 'Name three rivers of France.', provider='openai'/}

Image filters

filter / ascii The picture as text, a <pre> in place of the <img>: columns= characters across (64), as many lines as the picture's shape asks for, each character one of chars= - the lightest first (' .:-=+*#%@') - by the darkness of the part it stands for. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='ascii'/}
filter / atkinson Bill Atkinson's dither of the first Macintosh: like dither, but only three quarters of each pixel's error carried on, to six neighbours - lighter, higher contrast; levels= and colors= as dither's. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='atkinson'/}
filter / autocontrast The picture's tones stretched over the whole range: its darkest pixels made black and its lightest white, cutoff= percent (1) of them at each end let go first, so a grey, misty or faded picture gets its depth back - the colours keep their relations. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='autocontrast'/}
filter / bayer Ordered dithering: every pixel weighed against Bayer's threshold map of 8 by 8, the cross-hatch of an old screen; levels= and colors= as dither's. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='bayer'/}
filter / blur The picture out of focus by radius= CSS pixels (6), the same on the 2x picture. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='blur'/}
filter / blurhash A placeholder: Wolt's BlurHash of the picture in data-blurhash, and the hash decoded again as a small PNG behind the <img> - the blur of its colours the page shows until the picture has loaded. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='blurhash'/}
filter / dither Floyd and Steinberg's error diffusion: the picture in levels= greys (2, ink and paper alone) from the first of colors= to the second, every pixel's error carried to its neighbours not yet drawn; made at 1x, its pixels sharp, written as a PNG. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='dither'/}
filter / dominant A placeholder: the picture's dominant colour behind the <img> while it loads, and in data-color for a page's own use. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='dominant'/}
filter / duotone The picture in two colours: its luminance laid on the line from the first of colors= in the shadows to the second in the highlights ('#16213e, #f5c26b'). 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='duotone'/}
filter / edges The outlines of the picture: Sobel's operator, how fast its brightness changes across and down every pixel, drawn from the first of colors= where nothing changes to the second where the change is strongest - white lines on black, or '#fbfaf7, #1d1d1b' for a drawing in ink on paper; amount= percent (100) makes the lines stronger or fainter. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='edges'/}
filter / grayscale The picture in shades of grey, each pixel its luminance: 0.299 of its red, 0.587 of its green and 0.114 of its blue, the weights of television (GD's grayscale filter). 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='grayscale'/}
filter / halftone The picture as dots of ink on paper, an SVG in place of the <img>: a dot every cell= pixels (8) on rows set off by half a dot, its area the darkness there; the first of colors= the ink, the second the paper. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='halftone'/}
filter / invert The negative of the picture, every channel 255 less itself (GD's negate filter). 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='invert'/}
filter / lqip A placeholder: a low quality image of the picture, 16 pixels on its longer side and blurred, as a PNG in the page behind the <img> until the picture has loaded. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='lqip'/}
filter / pixelate The picture in blocks of cell= pixels (8), each block the average of what it covers (GD's pixelate filter, its advanced form); made at 1x and shown with its pixels sharp, written as a PNG unless format= says otherwise. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='pixelate'/}
filter / posterize Every colour channel cut to levels= steps (4), as a screen print of flat areas; written as a PNG unless format= says otherwise. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='posterize'/}
filter / sepia The brown of an old photograph: every pixel through the classic sepia matrix, amount= percent of the way from the picture to it (100). 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='sepia'/}
filter / sharpen The edges of the picture crisper by amount= percent (50): every pixel minus the pixels around it, a convolution of GD's. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='sharpen'/}
filter / solarize The Sabattier effect of the darkroom, a print flashed with light while it develops: every channel at threshold= percent (50) of its full value or more turned into its negative, 255 less itself, the rest left as it was - the highlights go dark and strange, the shadows stay. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='solarize'/}
filter / threshold The picture in two colours alone, a hard cut: every pixel whose luminance is threshold= percent (50) of white or more the second of colors= (paper), every other one the first (ink) - a stencil, a stamp, a scanned page made clean, where dither spreads the error on to keep the greys. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='threshold'/}
filter / thumbhash A placeholder: Evan Wallace's ThumbHash of the picture in data-thumbhash, and the hash decoded again as a small PNG behind the <img> - more of the picture than a BlurHash in fewer bytes, its proportion and its transparency kept. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='thumbhash'/}
filter / vignette The corners of the picture darker, as an old lens draws them, by amount= percent (50) at the very corner, the middle untouched. 
{pad:img 'photo.jpg', alt='A landscape', width=320, filter='vignette'/}

Holiday calendars

holidays / at Austria: the thirteen public holidays of the Feiertagsruhegesetz, the same in every state. 
{pad:holidays 'at', year=2026/}
holidays / be Belgium: the ten legal public holidays (wettelijke feestdagen, jours fériés légaux), their names in Dutch, French and German - lang= picks one, Dutch the default. 
{pad:holidays 'be', year=2026/}
holidays / br Brazil: the national holidays of federal law - Lei 662/1949 with Lei 10.607/2002 (1 January, 21 April, 1 May, 7 September, 2 and 15 November, 25 December), Lei 6.802/1980 (Our Lady of Aparecida, 12 October) and, since 2024, Lei 14.759/2023 (Zumbi and Black Consciousness Day, 20 November) - with Good Friday, which the federal government's yearly ordinance of holidays lists as a national one. 
{pad:holidays 'br', year=2026/}
holidays / ca Canada: the ten general holidays of the Canada Labour Code, the federal ones, their names in English and French - lang= picks one, English the default. 
{pad:holidays 'ca', year=2026/}
holidays / ch Switzerland: the four holidays every canton keeps - New Year's Day, Ascension Day, the Swiss National Day (1 August, the federal holiday by the constitution) and Christmas Day - their names in German, French and Italian, lang= picks one, German the default. 
{pad:holidays 'ch', year=2026/}
holidays / cz Czechia: the state holidays and other holidays of Act 245/2000 Sb., all of them days of rest (§ 3) - 1 January twice, as the Restoration Day of the Independent Czech State and as New Year's Day - with Good Friday since 2016 (Act 359/2015 Sb., in force from 21 December 2015). 
{pad:holidays 'cz', year=2026/}
holidays / de Germany: the nine holidays of every state, and with region= a state's own, by its ISO 3166-2 code - de-by is Bavaria. 
{pad:holidays 'de', year=2026/}
holidays / dk Denmark: the public holidays of the Danish church year (helligdage), Easter and Whit Sunday among them; Great Prayer Day, the fourth Friday after Easter, until 2023 - it was abolished from 2024. 
{pad:holidays 'dk', year=2026/}
holidays / es Spain: the national holidays (fiestas de ámbito nacional, Real Decreto 2001/1983): New Year's Day, Good Friday, Labour Day, Assumption Day, the National Day, All Saints' Day, Constitution Day, the Immaculate Conception and Christmas Day, and Epiphany, which a community may replace but every one keeps. 
{pad:holidays 'es', year=2026/}
holidays / fi Finland: the church holidays of the Church Act - New Year's Day, Epiphany, Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Monday, Ascension Day, Whit Sunday, Midsummer Day (the Saturday from 20 to 26 June), All Saints' Day (the Saturday from 31 October to 6 November), Christmas Day and Boxing Day - with May Day and Independence Day, the paid public holidays the University of Helsinki Almanac Office lists; Midsummer Eve and Christmas Eve are days off by many collective agreements, not by law - observances. 
{pad:holidays 'fi', year=2026/}
holidays / fr France: the eleven jours fériés of the Code du travail, exact since 1982, when 8 May became a holiday again. 
{pad:holidays 'fr', year=2026/}
holidays / gb The United Kingdom: the bank holidays of England and Wales, and with region= those of a nation by its ISO 3166-2 code - eng and wls the same, sct Scotland (2 January, the first Monday of August, St Andrew's Day; no Easter Monday), nir Northern Ireland (St Patrick's Day, the Battle of the Boyne). 
{pad:holidays 'gb', year=2026/}
holidays / hu Hungary: the rest days of the Labour Code (2012. 
{pad:holidays 'hu', year=2026/}
holidays / ie Ireland: the public holidays of the Organisation of Working Time Act, exact since 1994, when the May bank holiday came; St Brigid's Day since 2023 - the first Monday of February, or 1 February when that is a Friday - and the one-off Day of Remembrance and Recognition of 18 March 2022. 
{pad:holidays 'ie', year=2026/}
holidays / it Italy: the national public holidays (giorni festivi), Easter Sunday among them. 
{pad:holidays 'it', year=2026/}
holidays / jp Japan: the national holidays of the Act on National Holidays (国民の祝日に関する法律) and the one-off holidays of their own acts, with its two rules of days off: a holiday on a Sunday is made up for on the next day that is no holiday yet (振替休日, since 12 April 1973 - the next day until 2006, when no two holidays followed each other, so the same days), and a day between two holidays is one too (国民の休日, since 1986: 4 May from 1988 to 2006, and 22 September when Respect for the Aged Day falls on the 21st). 
{pad:holidays 'jp', year=2026/}
holidays / lu Luxembourg: the eleven legal public holidays, Europe Day (9 May) since 2019, their names in Luxembourgish, French and German - lang= picks one, Luxembourgish the default. 
{pad:holidays 'lu', year=2026/}
holidays / mx Mexico: the days of obligatory rest of the Ley Federal del Trabajo, art. 
{pad:holidays 'mx', year=2026/}
holidays / nl The Netherlands: the national holidays of the Algemene termijnenwet, with Easter and Whit Sunday, which fall on a Sunday anyway. 
{pad:holidays 'nl', year=2026/}
holidays / no Norway: the public holidays of the Public Holidays Act (helligdager) and the two national days of 1947 - 1 May and Constitution Day, 17 May - Easter and Whit Sunday among them; names in Bokmål. 
{pad:holidays 'no', year=2026/}
holidays / nz New Zealand: the public holidays of the Holidays Act 2003, s 44, and with region= the anniversary day of a province, by the ISO 3166-2 code of the region of its name - nz-auk Auckland, nz-wgn Wellington, nz-can Canterbury (Christchurch Show Day, the second Friday after the first Tuesday of November), nz-wtc Westland, nz-cit the Chatham Islands ... 
{pad:holidays 'nz', year=2026/}
holidays / pl Poland: the public holidays of the Act on Days Free from Work (ustawa o dniach wolnych od pracy), exact since 2011, when Epiphany came back, Easter and Pentecost Sunday among them; Christmas Eve since 2025, and the one-off 12 November 2018, a hundred years of independence. 
{pad:holidays 'pl', year=2026/}
holidays / pt Portugal: the thirteen mandatory holidays of the Código do Trabalho, art. 
{pad:holidays 'pt', year=2026/}
holidays / ro Romania: the legal holidays of the Labour Code (Legea 53/2003), art. 
{pad:holidays 'ro', year=2026/}
holidays / se Sweden: the public holidays of the Act on General Holidays (lag 1989:253), Easter and Whit Sunday among them; the National Day, 6 June, since 2005, when it replaced Whit Monday. 
{pad:holidays 'se', year=2026/}
holidays / sk Slovakia: the state holidays and days of rest of Act 241/1993 Z. 
{pad:holidays 'sk', year=2026/}
holidays / us The United States: the eleven federal holidays of 5 U.S.C. 
{pad:holidays 'us', year=2026/}
holidays / za South Africa: the twelve public holidays of the Public Holidays Act 36 of 1994. 
{pad:holidays 'za', year=2026/}

Search languages

search / da Danish: Snowball's stop words and its Danish stemmer as Snowball 3.1 has it (snowballstem.org/algorithms/danish), step for step after danish.sbl - a main suffix in R1 (an -s after an s-ending), the last letter of gd, dt, gt and kt, then -ig, -lig, -elig, -els and -løst (and the st of -igst before), a double consonant undoubled and an apostrophe at the end dropped: husene is hus, hurtigt hurt, venlighed ven, pc'en pc.

search / nl Dutch: Snowball's stop words and its Dutch stemmer as Snowball 3 has it - the algorithm of Wessel Kraaij and Renée Pohlmann (snowballstem.org/algorithms/dutch), step for step after dutch.sbl: plurals, diminutives and adjective endings off, a vowel lengthened where the spelling shortened it, the ge- of a participle dropped - maken and maak are maak, huisjes huis, gelopen loop.

search / no Norwegian: Snowball's stop words and its Norwegian stemmer as Snowball 3.1 has it (snowballstem.org/algorithms/norwegian), for Bokmål and Nynorsk alike - the locales nb and nn search in it too - step for step after norwegian.sbl: a main suffix in R1 (-ers not after the letters that keep it, -s after an s-ending, an r not after an e or a k after a consonant, -ert and -erte as -er), the t of dt and vt, then -leg, -lig, -els, -lov ..., and an apostrophe at the end dropped: husene is hus, barna barn, hyggelig hygg.

Data formats

format / atom Atom (RFC 4287), written: a feed with its id, title, updated and author, an entry per row - its id, title, updated, link, summary and content (title, link, date, summary, body and id of a row, or the front matter of a Markdown collection: subs/formats/_lib/feeds.php). 
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'atom', $rows );
format / csv Comma separated values (RFC 4180), read and written: the reader is the engine's own, data/csv.php - a header line naming the fields, then a row per line - and the writer the one a CSV page answer is made with: a header row of every key the rows use, a cell holding a list as its JSON, and a text cell a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, +, -, @ in front) with a ' before it. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'csv', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'csv', $rows );
format / geojson GeoJSON (RFC 7946), read and written: a feature a row - its properties, its id, geometry (the type), lat and lon of a Point, coordinates of any other - and rows as a FeatureCollection, a Point for every row with lat and lon, the other fields its properties. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'geojson', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'geojson', $rows );
format / gpx GPS Exchange Format 1.1, read and written: every point a row - the waypoints, the points of the routes, those of the track segments - with its type, track, segment, point, name, lat, lon, ele, time and desc; rows as waypoints, routes and tracks again, by their type (as='track' makes a list of positions one track). 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'gpx', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'gpx', $rows );
format / ics ICalendar (RFC 5545), read and written: the VEVENTs of a calendar as rows - uid, summary, start, end, allday, timezone, location, description, url, status, categories, rrule - and rows as a calendar, folded at 75 octets with CRLF line ends, its UID and DTSTAMP made of the rows so the same rows give the same bytes. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'ics', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'ics', $rows );
format / ini INI files, read and written: [sections] of key = value lines, ; and # comments, quoted values, key[] lists and key[name] records. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'ini', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'ini', $rows );
format / json JSON (RFC 8259), read and written: the reader is the engine's own, data/json.php, which takes the document out of the text around it; the writer writes any value as a JSON page answer has it - pretty, slashes and characters past ASCII as they are. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'json', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'json', $rows );
format / jsonfeed JSON Feed 1.1 (jsonfeed.org), written: the feed's title=, link=, self=, description=, author= and an item per row - its id, url, title, content_html or content_text, summary and date_published (title, link, date, summary, body and id of a row, or the front matter of a Markdown collection: subs/formats/_lib/feeds.php). 
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'jsonfeed', $rows );
format / jsonseq JSON text sequences (RFC 7464), read and written: a record a row - an RS (0x1E), a JSON text, a line feed - as jq --seq writes them and a GeoJSON text sequence (RFC 8142) is made of; a record that is no JSON, or a number cut short, is the error under the strict check and passed over on the lenient walk, as the RFC has a parser recover (subs/formats/_lib/jsonseq.php). 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'jsonseq', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'jsonseq', $rows );
format / kml KML (OGC KML 2.2), read and written: a Placemark a row - its ExtendedData, id, name, description, folder, address, style, time, and its geometry as GeoJSON's reader has it: geometry, lat and lon of a Point, coordinates of any other (subs/formats/_lib/kml.php) - and rows as a Document of placemarks, in folders by their folder, Points written from lat and lon. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'kml', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'kml', $rows );
format / markdown Markdown pipe tables (GitHub Flavored Markdown), read and written: the first table of a text - a README, a page of notes - as rows, and rows as a table whose columns line up, numbers on the right. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'markdown', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'markdown', $rows );
format / ndjson Newline delimited JSON (JSON Lines): a JSON value a line, a row each, read and written - what a log, a stream or a bulk export is made of. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'ndjson', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'ndjson', $rows );
format / rss RSS 2.0, written: a channel of the feed's title=, link= and description=, an item per row - its title, link, date, summary and id (title, link, date, summary, body and id of a row, or the front matter of a Markdown collection: subs/formats/_lib/feeds.php). 
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'rss', $rows );
format / srt SubRip subtitles (SRT, as the Library of Congress describes it, fdd000569), read and written: a subtitle a row, as WebVTT's cues are - id (its number), start, end, startms, endms, text, plain, voice and settings (subs/formats/_lib/cues.php) - and rows as subtitles numbered from 1 in the order of their start, 00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:04,000, with CRLF line ends. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'srt', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'srt', $rows );
format / toml TOML 1.0, read and written: tables, arrays of tables, inline tables, dotted keys, every kind of string, number and date. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'toml', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'toml', $rows );
format / tsv Tab separated values (IANA text/tab-separated-values), read and written: a header line of field names, then a row per line, the cells split at the tabs. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'tsv', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'tsv', $rows );
format / vcf VCard 4.0 (RFC 6350), read and written - 3.0 cards are read as well: a card a row, name, the parts of the name, org, title, email and phone (the preferred one, and emails and phones all of them), url, the parts of the address, birthday, note and uid; rows as version 4.0 cards, folded at 75 octets with CRLF line ends, a UID made of the row when it has none. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'vcf', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'vcf', $rows );
format / vtt WebVTT (W3C, WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format), read and written: a cue a row - id, start, end, startms, endms, text, plain, voice and settings (subs/formats/_lib/cues.php) - and rows as the cues of a <track>, sorted by their start: ?talk&padFormat=vtt is the src of a video's captions or chapters. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'vtt', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'vtt', $rows );
format / xlsx Excel spreadsheets (Office Open XML, SpreadsheetML), written and read with PHP's zip extension: rows as a workbook of one sheet - a bold header row frozen at the top, numbers as numbers, booleans as booleans, dates with a date format, every text a text and never a formula - the same bytes for the same rows; and the first sheet of a workbook as rows - shared and inline strings, numbers, booleans, dates (sheet= picks another, by name or number). 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'xlsx', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'xlsx', $rows );
format / xml XML, read only: the reader is the engine's own, data/xml.php - an element's attributes and children its fields, a repeated element a list, the names of every namespace taken. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'xml', $contents );
format / yaml YAML 1.2, read and written with the PHP yaml extension: the reader is the engine's own, data/yaml.php - true and false the only booleans, 9:30 a text and not 570 - and the writer yaml_emit's document between --- and ..., a text that would read as another kind of value quoted. 
$rows = padFormatRead ( 'yaml', $contents );
$contents = padFormatWrite ( 'yaml', $rows );

Themes

theme / blueprint White lines on the deep blue of a cyanotype drawing: a faint grid on the page, a fine one every 20 pixels and a stronger one every 100 as on drawing paper, the headings lettered in capitals as a title block is, the links the yellow of an engineer's marking pencil - for technical pages, demos and diagrams. 
{widget:theme 'blueprint'}<p>A box in the blueprint theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / contrast Black on white, a dark blue for the links: every text of the frame at 7 to 1 or more, WCAG AAA, the links underlined and the focus ringed thick, so colour is never all that tells them apart. 
{widget:theme 'contrast'}<p>A box in the contrast theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / contrast-dark White on black, yellow for the links, as the high-contrast black scheme of an operating system has them: the dark counterpart of contrast, every text of the frame at 7 to 1 or more, WCAG AAA, the links underlined, the focus ringed thick in yellow and the lines light enough to be seen. 
{widget:theme 'contrast-dark'}<p>A box in the contrast-dark theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / dark The frame's own dark colours, kept dark whatever the system or the frame's switch says, the side's headings lightened to WCAG AA. 
{widget:theme 'dark'}<p>A box in the dark theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / forest A light page in the greens of leaves, a deep forest-green side and accent. 
{widget:theme 'forest'}<p>A box in the forest theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / light The frame's own light colours, kept light whatever the system or the frame's switch says, with the two greys and the soft accent the frame's set has below WCAG AA - its dim text, the side's headings, a link on the accent's tint - darkened to it. 
{widget:theme 'light'}<p>A box in the light theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / mono Greys only, black links underlined and black buttons: a page whose colour is all in its pictures and charts. 
{widget:theme 'mono'}<p>A box in the mono theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / newspaper Black on newsprint, a deep red for the links and a serif for every line, the headings set tight as a paper's are. 
{widget:theme 'newspaper'}<p>A box in the newspaper theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / night A dark page for reading late, in warm colours alone: parchment text on a brown-black ground, an amber accent, the messages in olive, gold and coral - every colour's blue below its red and its green, as a screen's night mode shifts away from blue light. 
{widget:theme 'night'}<p>A box in the night theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / ocean Deep navy water under a pale blue text, the links the cyan of a shallow lagoon. 
{widget:theme 'ocean'}<p>A box in the ocean theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / paper Warm off-white paper and soft black ink, a blue-black accent like a fountain pen's, the type a book face: quiet pages for reading. 
{widget:theme 'paper'}<p>A box in the paper theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / readable A page set for readers with dyslexia, after the British Dyslexia Association's Dyslexia Style Guide: dark text on cream rather than black on white, a plain, evenly spaced sans-serif (Atkinson Hyperlegible where it is installed, else the guide's Verdana, Tahoma or Trebuchet), 16 pixels, the lines 1.6 apart, the letters .06em and the words .16em further apart - within what WCAG 1.4.12 asks a page to bear - paragraphs no wider than 70 characters, bold instead of italics, no block capitals in the side's headings, and the messages in Okabe and Ito's blue, orange and vermilion, darkened to AA: no green and no red, which the guide asks to avoid for colour-blind readers. 
{widget:theme 'readable'}<p>A box in the readable theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / sepia The browns of an old photograph, dark umber on a parchment page and a saddle-brown accent: easy on the eyes for a long read. 
{widget:theme 'sepia'}<p>A box in the sepia theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / solarized-dark The deep blue-green and cream of Solarized's dark mode: its base tones for the page, the panels, the side and the code, its blue for the links, its green, yellow and red for the messages. 
{widget:theme 'solarized-dark'}<p>A box in the solarized-dark theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / solarized-light The cream and blue-green of Solarized's light mode: its base tones for the page, the side and the code, its blue for the links, its green, yellow and red for the messages. 
{widget:theme 'solarized-light'}<p>A box in the solarized-light theme.</p>{/widget:theme}
theme / terminal Green phosphor on black with an amber accent, every letter monospaced, as an old video terminal showed it. 
{widget:theme 'terminal'}<p>A box in the terminal theme.</p>{/widget:theme}

Colour palettes

palette / batlow Fabio Crameri's sequential scale batlow, from a dark navy through teal, a moss green, olive and ochre to salmon and a pale pink: perceptually uniform, its lightness rising all the way, so it prints as a ramp in grey, and read by colour-vision-deficient and colour-blind eyes, as Crameri's scientific colour maps all are. 
{widget:palette 'batlow'/}
palette / blues ColorBrewer's single-hue sequential scale of nine blues, from nearly white to navy (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'blues'/}
palette / brbg ColorBrewer's diverging scale of eleven classes from brown through a light grey to blue-green, readable by colour-blind eyes (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'brbg'/}
palette / cividis A perceptually uniform scale from navy to yellow made to look alike to people with and without a red-green colour vision deficiency (Nuñez, Anderton and Renslow, 2018). 
{widget:palette 'cividis'/}
palette / dark2 ColorBrewer's qualitative Dark2, eight deep colours to tell categories apart - teal green, orange, slate violet, magenta, green, mustard, brown and grey (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org): darker and more saturated than its pastels, so thin lines and small marks stay visible on a light surface; ColorBrewer marks its first three safe for colour-blind eyes, four to six possibly, more not. 
{widget:palette 'dark2'/}
palette / earth Eight tones of soil, clay, moss and sand, PAD's own qualitative palette: umber, olive, ochre, slate, sienna, moss, sand and a dark brown - quiet colours for a page in warm tones. 
{widget:palette 'earth'/}
palette / glasbey Thirty-two colours to tell many categories apart, each chosen as far as it can be from all before it, by the method of Chris Glasbey, Gerie van der Heijden, Vivian Toh and others ("Colour displays for categorical images", Color Research and Application 32.4, 2007): started from white and black, so none is near either, and no grey among them, every colour of a chroma of 20 or more. 
{widget:palette 'glasbey'/}
palette / greens ColorBrewer's single-hue sequential scale of nine greens, from nearly white to a deep forest green (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'greens'/}
palette / greys ColorBrewer's sequential scale of nine greys, from white to black (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'greys'/}
palette / inferno A perceptually uniform scale from black through purple, red and orange to a pale yellow, of the matplotlib family of viridis. 
{widget:palette 'inferno'/}
palette / magma A perceptually uniform scale from black through purple and red to a pale yellow, of the matplotlib family of viridis. 
{widget:palette 'magma'/}
palette / okabe-ito The eight colours Masataka Okabe and Kei Ito chose to stay apart for every kind of colour vision (Color Universal Design, 2008): orange, sky blue, bluish green, yellow, blue, vermillion, reddish purple and black - black put last here, where the original lists it first, as it vanishes on a dark surface. 
{widget:palette 'okabe-ito'/}
palette / oranges ColorBrewer's single-hue sequential scale of nine oranges, from cream to a dark burnt orange (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'oranges'/}
palette / paired ColorBrewer's qualitative Paired, twelve colours in six pairs, a light and a dark of one hue each - blue, green, red, orange, purple, and a pale yellow with a brown (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org): for categories that come in pairs - last year and this, planned and done - the pair's hue telling the group and its lightness the member; ColorBrewer marks it safe for colour-blind eyes up to four colours, possibly to eight, more not. 
{widget:palette 'paired'/}
palette / pastel ColorBrewer's Pastel1, nine light qualitative colours for large areas behind dark text - a background, a map, the fills of a treemap (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'pastel'/}
palette / piyg ColorBrewer's diverging scale of eleven classes from pink through a light grey to yellow-green, readable by colour-blind eyes (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'piyg'/}
palette / plasma A perceptually uniform scale from deep blue through magenta and orange to yellow, of the matplotlib family of viridis. 
{widget:palette 'plasma'/}
palette / puor ColorBrewer's diverging scale PuOr of eleven classes, from a dark brown through orange to a light grey middle and on through lilac to a dark purple (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org), in ColorBrewer's order, its orange end first: orange against purple, two hues red-green colour-blind eyes still tell apart, and ColorBrewer marks it safe for them. 
{widget:palette 'puor'/}
palette / rdbu ColorBrewer's diverging scale of eleven classes from dark red through a light grey to dark blue, for values on both sides of a middle - colder and warmer, less and more (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org). 
{widget:palette 'rdbu'/}
palette / rdylbu ColorBrewer's diverging scale RdYlBu of eleven classes, from a dark red through orange to a pale yellow middle and on through light blue to a dark indigo (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org), for values on both sides of a middle - hotter and colder, above and below: the spread of a rainbow, but ColorBrewer marks it safe for colour-blind eyes at every number of classes, where its Spectral and RdYlGn are at most possibly so, and only up to five. 
{widget:palette 'rdylbu'/}
palette / romao Fabio Crameri's cyclic scale romaO, for what goes round - an angle, a direction, the hour, the month: from a dark plum through brick, ochre and a pale yellow, a pale green, sky blue and indigo back to the plum, its last colour next to its first. 
{widget:palette 'romao'/}
palette / tol-bright Paul Tol's bright qualitative scheme of seven colours, told apart by colour-blind eyes and in print: blue, red, green, yellow, cyan, purple and grey, in his order (from the colors.json of his tol_colors package). 
{widget:palette 'tol-bright'/}
palette / tol-muted Paul Tol's muted qualitative scheme of ten colours, softer than the bright one and still told apart by colour-blind eyes: rose, indigo, sand, green, cyan, wine, teal, olive, purple and a pale grey, in his order (from the colors.json of his tol_colors package). 
{widget:palette 'tol-muted'/}
palette / tol-vibrant Paul Tol's vibrant qualitative scheme of seven colours, made for TensorBoard and told apart by colour-blind eyes: orange, blue, cyan, magenta, red, teal and grey, in his order (from the colors.json of his tol_colors package). 
{widget:palette 'tol-vibrant'/}
palette / turbo Google's rainbow made smooth, by Anton Mikhailov (2019): from a dark indigo through blue, cyan, green, yellow and orange to a dark red, every step a visible change of hue, for a depth map or a field where the eye must read a value at a glance. 
{widget:palette 'turbo'/}
palette / vik Fabio Crameri's diverging scale vik, from a dark navy through blue and a pale blue to a light middle and on through tan and rust to a dark red-brown, for values on both sides of a middle: perceptually uniform, its two halves nearly alike in lightness, and read by colour-vision-deficient and colour-blind eyes, as Crameri's scientific colour maps all are. 
{widget:palette 'vik'/}
palette / viridis A perceptually uniform scale from dark purple through blue and green to yellow, the default of matplotlib (Stéfan van der Walt and Nathaniel Smith, 2015): even steps look even, it prints in grey as a ramp, and the common forms of colour blindness read it. 
{widget:palette 'viridis'/}
palette / ylgnbu ColorBrewer's multi-hue sequential scale YlGnBu of nine classes, from a pale yellow through green and teal to blue and a dark navy (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org): its hue turns as its lightness falls, so the steps of a map or a heatmap tell apart better than in one hue, and ColorBrewer marks it safe for colour-blind eyes. 
{widget:palette 'ylgnbu'/}
palette / ylorrd ColorBrewer's multi-hue sequential scale YlOrRd of nine classes, from a pale yellow through orange and red to a dark crimson (Cynthia Brewer, colorbrewer2.org), for heat, risk or intensity: its hue turns as its lightness falls, and ColorBrewer marks it safe for colour-blind eyes. 
{widget:palette 'ylorrd'/}
